name: Radio
statusNote: Stable in use; alpha is Primer's label. It is the bare 16px circle; label and layout come from FormControl and grouping from RadioGroup.
summary: A 16px circle for one choice among mutually exclusive options sharing a name. Use it inside a RadioGroup with a FormControl per option; choose Checkbox for independent choices and SegmentedControl for a compact view switch.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: A value never shown, identifying this option in the group and the form.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: The group name; radios sharing a name are exclusive. Taken from RadioGroup when not given.

inputs.name: checked
inputs.description: Whether this option is chosen. Controlled when given; otherwise defaultChecked seeds it.

inputs.name: required
inputs.description: Some radio in the name group must be chosen to submit. FormControl strips it from an individual radio; set it on RadioGroup.

inputs.name: onChange
inputs.description: Called when this radio becomes checked.

anatomy.name: Circle
anatomy.description: A 16px circle with a 1px --control-borderColor-emphasis ring inside it and a --bgColor-default fill.

anatomy.name: Dot
anatomy.description: When checked, the ring thickens to 4px of --control-checked-bgColor-rest, leaving an 8px --control-checked-fgColor-rest centre: the 'dot' is the fill showing through, not a separate shape.

layout.text: The circle is exactly 16px, ring included, with 2px of top margin that centres it on a 20px text line beside it and no other margin.
Checked, the ring is 4px wide inside the 16px box, so the centre is an 8px disc.

states.text: Fill --control-checked-fgColor-rest, ring 4px of --control-checked-bgColor-rest (the background token, so dark high-contrast shows no separate border colour).
Keyboard focus only: a 2px solid --focus-outline-color outline 2px outside the circle, no shadow. The outline follows the circle's round shape.
Unchecked: fill --control-bgColor-disabled, ring --control-borderColor-disabled. Checked: centre --control-checked-fgColor-disabled, 4px ring --control-checked-bgColor-disabled. Not-allowed cursor.

behaviour.text: Choosing a radio checks it and unchecks the other radios with the same name; a checked radio cannot be unchecked by pressing it again.
The ring colour transitions over 80ms cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1); the ring width and the fill change instantly, so the dot appears at once.
Its name comes from the name prop, else from the enclosing RadioGroup; a radio with neither warns, since it would not be exclusive with anything.

keyboard: Tab enters the group at the checked radio (or the first, if none is checked) and Tab again leaves it; the group is one tab stop.
Arrow keys move to the next or previous enabled radio in the name group and check it, wrapping at the ends.
semantics: Checked state is the radio's own; the group is named by RadioGroup's legend.

notes.text: Exclusivity by name, single-tab-stop roving focus and arrow-key selection are the browser's behaviour for <input type=radio>; Radio adds none of it. A native build implements the group model: one tab stop, arrows move and check, wrap at the ends, skip disabled radios.

aria-checked is set from the checked prop, so an uncontrolled radio carries aria-checked=false even after the user checks it; browsers expose the native state, which is what a native build should expose.
transition: background-color, border-color 80ms ... gives background-color no duration, so the fill snaps; only the ring colour fades.

The forced-colours rule (CanvasText fill and border) is not scoped to :checked, so under forced colours every radio, checked or not, draws as a filled disc and the states look alike. A native high-contrast build should fill only the checked one.

The dot is the 8px of fill left inside a 4px ring, in --control-checked-fgColor-rest (white, off-white in dark dimmed); dark themes do not darken it. Disabled-checked turns it --control-checked-fgColor-disabled, which is near-black in dark themes.
No hover or pressed colour, and the target is the 16px circle alone; the FormControl label extends it in practice.
The 80ms duration and curve and the focus outline's 2px width and offset are literals.
No size change for a coarse pointer.
